land.text: Spanish Guinea: Bioko (Fernando Po), Annobón and the mainland Río Muni, with the Corisco and Elobey islands

predecessors.note: The Spanish Guinea page: 'On 12 October 1968, Spain conceded the independence of the Republic of Equatorial Guinea.' Cliopatria's Francoist Spain shape still reaches 11.27 E, 0.93 N (the Guinea coast) until 1972 and its Equatorial Guinea row begins 1969; see notes.

capitals.name: Malabo (Santa Isabel)
capitals.note: 'Independence from Spain was gained on 12 October 1968, at noon in the country's then capital, Malabo'; the Spanish Guinea page gives 'Capital: Santa Isabel' and no rename date. Coordinates from the gazetteer (Natural Earth). The capital became Ciudad de la Paz (1 35 20 N, 10 49 21 E, the page's infobox) in January 2026, after the map's last year.

correction.text: Spanish Guinea as the independent Republic of Equatorial Guinea from 12 October 1968, the same land as the 1969 shape

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: Cliopatria's Equatorial Guinea row begins 1969 but 'Independence from Spain was gained on 12 October 1968'. Cliopatria's Francoist Spain shape still covers this land through 1972.

correction.text: the shape plus Annobón Province, 'the insular Annobón Province, which is about 155 km south of the equator'; 'The insular region consists of the islands of Bioko (formerly Fernando Po) in the Gulf of Guinea and Annobón'

keyframe_review.note: 28,557 km2 against the infobox 'Total: 28,050 km2' (ratio 1.02), so the area is right. But the shape's bounding box (0.93-3.82 N) stops north of the equator and omits Annobón, a province of the country; the gazetteer resolves Annobón to 0 cells at its resolution, so the correction is in the record rather than on the map until the grid or a radius can hold a very small island. Mainland: 107 shape cells against 112 for modern Equatorial Guinea.
Same 28,557 km2 shape. The 19 May 2025 ICJ ruling on Mbanié, Cocoteros and Conga islands is later than the shape and confirms Equatorial Guinea's title (see wars).

region.text: the colony of Spanish Guinea: 'Formerly the colony of Spanish Guinea, its post-independence name refers to its location'; Bioko, Annobón, Río Muni

ledger.note: 12 October 1968: Spanish Guinea becomes the independent Equatorial Guinea. 'Independence from Spain was gained on 12 October 1968, at noon in the country's then capital, Malabo.' Spanish Guinea page: 'Spain formally handed power to the new government on 12 October 1968' (its infobox says 13 October, its text 12 October). Autonomy had come earlier: 'A decision of 9 August 1963, approved by a referendum of 15 December 1963, gave the territory a measure of autonomy'.

wars.name: Mbanié Island dispute (Gabon and Equatorial Guinea)
wars.outcome: 'On 19 May 2025 the International Court of Justice (ICJ) granted Equatorial Guinea sovereignty over Mbanie Island, Cocoteros Island, and Conga Island', 'in response to territorial claims that neighbouring Gabon had been making since 1972'.
wars.note: A sovereignty dispute over islets in Corisco Bay ('Corisco and the two Elobey islands are in Corisco Bay, on the border of Río Muni and Gabon'), not a war; no troops or ground are described. Listed so the reviewer sees it was considered. The islets are far below the grid's resolution, so there is no contest zone and no ledger event. The page does not say when the dispute began beyond 'since 1972'. Span clamped by the reviewer to the dossier's last year (the ICJ ruling of 19 May 2025 falls after it).

certainty.note: Río Muni was fixed by the Treaty of Paris: 'The eventual treaty of Paris in 1900 left Spain with the continental enclave of Río Muni' (Spanish Guinea page: 'Definitive territorial delimitation by the Treaty of Paris: 1900'); the island frontier is the coast. The Corisco Bay islets were disputed with Gabon until the ICJ ruling of 19 May 2025.

notes: Wikidata: Cliopatria gives this row Q983, the id it also gives the Guinea row (slug guinea, 1960-2024, written by another part of the group). The two rows lie in different places (Guinea's centroid is 10.9 W, 10.4 N and its modern countries are Guinea, Mali and Ivory Coast; this row's centroid is 10.1 E, 1.7 N), so they are different states: one dossier each, no merge. Cliopatria's Francoist Spain rows francoist-spain_1961 (1961-1972) keep a bounding box reaching 11.27 E and 0.93 N, i.e. Spanish Guinea, four years after independence, and the 1973 shape drops it; Francoist Spain (eu-21) should end its claim on this land at 12 October 1968 and carry the matching loss to equatorial-guinea. Annobón (south of the equator) is outside Cliopatria's shape and invisible to the gazetteer at its resolution. The Spanish Guinea page gives independence as 13 October 1968 in its infobox and 12 October in the text; the Equatorial Guinea page agrees with 12 October. The pages opened do not date the renaming of Santa Isabel as Malabo or of Fernando Po (the EG page only says 'formerly Fernando Po'); capital kept as 'Malabo (Santa Isabel)'. Obiang's coup of 3 August 1979 ('deposed his uncle on 3 August 1979') moved no land. Rulers omitted. Page budget: two pages. native_names left empty: no page read gives one.
